doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Giuffre's rhythm section and the 'You and Lee' album
summary: They talk about the Giuffre sessions rhythm players and the brass album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Anyway, just to finish off the record with Giuffre and the sax section, you said you don’t remember how the rhythm section got hired for that?
Yeah. I didn’t suggest [it]. I didn’t know the bass player I don’t think.
I don’t know what the connection [was]. I guess Giuffre knew him from someplace.

My favorite cut from that record is that long chart on Cork and Bib, “The Blues”. It’s an amazing chart and an amazing performance. Just the concept of that sax section is just so different from standard saxophone section writing and I think it just jibed with the way you played and the way Warne played there’s just something very special about it for me.
Jimmy was certainly sympathetic with that music.
Now the next record. The one called You and Lee with a brass section and Bill Evans, Sonny Dallas, and Roy Haynes that Giuffre also did in October of that
Boy, I haven’t heard that one in a long time. I don’t know if I own that record.
That one, I confess, I haven’t heard. It looks promising certainly, with the players and the writing.
It was nice. Apparently Sonny Dallas was very uncomfortable with Giuffre. I heard him really criticizing the way Giuffre treated him. Bill Evans was reading the paper between tunes.
Like Ron Carter was doing at a date that he did with us.
With Sal Mosca and Mousie Alexander.
